items.question: What is the core thing a VPC gives you?
options: Network isolation — your private section of AWS with walls you control
Free unlimited AdministratorAccess for every engineer
Automatic deletion of all databases every night
A replacement for IAM Users and Policies
items.ren_hint_english: Virtual Private Cloud — isolation is the product.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: VPC = private isolated network — walls + doors neenga control panreenga.
items.explanation: A VPC is your isolated slice of AWS networking. You decide IP ranges, what faces the internet, and traffic rules.

items.question: Where should an internet-facing API server and a user database live?
options: API in a public subnet; database in a private subnet
Both in a public subnet with open 0.0.0.0/0 on every port
Both in a private subnet with no path for users at all
Database in a public subnet; API only in a private subnet
items.ren_hint_english: Public faces users. Database never faces the internet.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: API = public subnet. Database = private subnet — always.
items.explanation: API needs to receive user traffic (public). Database is reached only by the API inside the VPC (private).

items.question: In the AWS console, how do you prove a subnet is truly public?
options: Its route table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an Internet Gateway
The subnet name contains the word 'public'
Someone said it is public in Slack
It has a Security Group attached
items.ren_hint_english: Labels lie — the route table is the proof.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: Subnet name illa — Route Table-la IGW route irundha thaan public.
items.explanation: A public subnet routes internet traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to an Internet Gateway. No IGW route means it is effectively private.

items.situation: You are deploying a web app: an API that handles user requests, and a database with accounts and order history.
items.question: What Security Group rule should the database have?
options: Allow inbound only from the API server's Security Group — never from the whole internet
Allow inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on the database port for convenience
Disable all Security Groups so nothing blocks traffic
Allow SSH from the entire internet on port 22
items.ren_hint_english: Database SG = wall inside the wall — only API may talk to it.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: DB Security Group — API SG mattum allow. Internet-ku open pannaadheenga.
items.explanation: Least network privilege: DB accepts traffic only from the API. Opening 0.0.0.0/0 on a DB port is a classic breach path.

items.situation: A developer asks: 'Open port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 on the EC2 Security Group so I can SSH easily.'
items.question: What do you do?
options: Decline — offer Session Manager, or SSH locked to their specific IP only
Open 22 to the world because velocity matters more than security
Move the database into a public subnet instead
Delete the VPC so networking is simpler
items.ren_hint_english: 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH = entire internet can knock. Safer paths exist.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: Port 22 → 0.0.0.0/0 = full internet attack surface. Decline pannunga.
items.explanation: Opening SSH to the world is scanned constantly. Prefer Systems Manager Session Manager, or restrict SSH to a known IP.

items.situation: Day 3 rule with no exceptions: databases must not be reachable from the public internet.
items.question: Which subnet type should a database always use? (Type: public or private)
items.ren_hint_english: No public entrance for the server room.
items.explanation: Databases always live in private subnets — no public IP, no direct internet path.
